answer: A seniority ladder ties each key's reward share to unbroken graded work. Every epoch a key answers an assigned topic, such as how rain carves karst caves, and a 5-seat jury scores it. Each pass adds one rung; a miss or failing score drops the key to zero. The ledger records each streak's anchor epoch, so no key can claim rungs it never earned. A key earns rung/28 of a full reward and reaches the summit only after 28 straight passes, about a week. A farm of 1,000 fake keys must write 28,000 original passing answers before any earns full pay.
